decisions.executionNote: Approach the left end of the horizontal mallet with the left arm, lifting and gradually orienting downward. Geometry estimated from calibrated head image.
Continue above the mallet handle while aligning the gripper's long axis with the shaft; right arm stays parked.
Finish downward orientation and descend toward the handle, stopping above the estimated grasp height for visual alignment.
Correct the small wrist-view lateral offset, lower to the handle, and close the left gripper. Retention will be checked by lifting.
The shaft is off-center in the wrist view; reopen and correct in the opposite lateral direction before reclosing, rather than assuming a grasp.
Finish closing, then lift vertically to test whether the handle is retained. Watch the mallet independently of reported gripper command.
Mallet is centered between the fingers after lifting. Move it above the leftmost key with clearance, keeping the left EE in its own workspace.
Raise further and move the mallet toward the leftmost red key; apparent tip height is uncertain, so establish clear overhead clearance before descending.
Replan from the interrupted pose with smaller increments, moving left and forward while lowering from the high folded posture. Keep the tip clear of the keys.
Align the retained mallet tip with the red leftmost key while descending conservatively. The tip-to-wrist offset is being refined from the live views.
Make a short controlled strike on the leftmost red key, then lift vertically 4 cm before advancing to the next key.
The lift was interrupted near a folded reach limit. Complete clearance with small backward/right motions, then advance one key spacing toward orange while retaining the mallet.
Fine-align with the second orange key and make a vertical strike; maintain closed grip and pause briefly at the bottom for visual checking.
Lift the mallet 4 cm after the orange strike, then move one key spacing right to yellow, keeping the left arm on the left side.
Strike the third, yellow key and lift vertically by 4 cm before any lateral movement.
After the yellow-key lift, advance to the fourth green key and strike vertically, without sweeping across the keys at contact height.
Lift clear by 4.5 cm after green, then align over the fifth light-blue key. Mallet remains visible in the closed left gripper.
Strike the fifth light-blue key vertically, then lift by 4.75 cm before advancing. Maintain closed grip and configuration continuity.
Advance at clearance to the sixth dark-blue key, then strike vertically. The mallet remains visibly retained; keep the other arm parked.
Lift 4.8 cm after the sixth key, with a slight rearward adjustment for reach margin, then advance to the seventh purple key.
Replan from the interrupted pose: use small rightward and rearward increments while slightly lowering to avoid the folded reach limit, aligning over purple with clearance.
Strike the seventh purple key at the current alignment, then lift vertically 4 cm before moving to the final key.
Move at clearance to the final magenta key, with a small rearward wrist adjustment and shaft yaw correction to retain reach margin and tip alignment.
Strike the eighth, rightmost magenta key and then lift vertically 4.25 cm, completing the intended left-to-right sequence with clearance after the final hit.
Increase final tip clearance substantially while retreating for reach margin. The episode is still active, so completion is not assumed from the commanded sequence.
Return above the left end for a more deliberate sequence with greater actual tip lift. Rotate the shaft diagonally so the wrist can remain farther back with safe elbow-up reach.
Complete the high-clearance return to the red key while bringing the mallet shaft diagonally forward. This permits larger lifts without the previous folded-reach limit.
Establish a visibly clear lift over the left end and refine the tip height from its motion, before a more deliberate contact-and-lift sequence.
Bring the tip forward over the leftmost red key and lower from the high-clearance pose. Stop above the expected contact height for visual confirmation.
Make a deliberate first-key strike with a short bottom pause. The following lift will be substantially larger than the minimum to ensure the tip actually clears.
Lift straight up 12 cm after the red-key contact, without lateral motion, to establish unambiguous tip clearance before proceeding right.
The red-key lift is visibly clear. Advance one key pitch to orange at height, then make a deliberate vertical strike with a brief bottom pause.
Lift nearly 12 cm after the orange contact, then advance to yellow only after achieving clearance. The tip is visually on the orange bar at the start.
Refine yellow-key alignment from the tip image, then strike vertically with a brief bottom pause. Keep the mallet closed in the left gripper.
Lift 12 cm after the yellow-key contact, then advance one key pitch to green only at clearance. Continue the deliberate left-to-right sequence.
Strike the fourth green key vertically from clear height, then pause briefly at contact. The next motion will lift before any sideways advance.
Lift vertically 12 cm after the green strike and briefly stabilize, checking mallet retention and actual tip clearance before advancing.
With the green-key lift visibly clear, move right to the fifth light-blue key, strike vertically, and briefly pause at the bottom.
Lift 12 cm after the fifth light-blue key, then move one pitch right to dark blue while the tip is clear.
Fine-align over the sixth dark-blue key, descend vertically for a deliberate strike, and pause briefly before lifting.
Lift 12 cm after the sixth dark-blue contact, then advance at clearance to the seventh purple key.
Fine-align over the seventh purple key, then strike straight down and briefly pause at contact before the required lift.
The previous descent was rejected before execution. Replan from the observed pose with smaller vertical increments to strike the seventh purple key.
Finish the purple-key contact with a small settling motion, then lift straight up 11.2 cm before moving to the final key.
The purple-key lift is visibly clear. Move one pitch to the final magenta key and approach vertically, retaining a small contact-height margin for alignment.
Replan the rejected descent from the observed pose using smaller initial increments, then strike the final magenta key vertically.
